partners.mechanism_chain: APC (HGNC:421) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway (WP:WP471); Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway (WP:WP471) —LEADS_TO→ Leukocytosis (HP:0001898); Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway (WP:WP471) —LEADS_TO→ Colorectal adenoma (HP:0030058); Colorectal adenoma (HP:0030058) —LEADS_TO→ Colorectal cancer (MONDO:0005575); Leukocytosis (HP:0001898) —LEADS_TO→ Juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia (MONDO:0011908). Loss-of-function mutations in the Adenomatous Polyposis Coli (APC) gene disrupt the Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway. This dysregulation leads to the accumulation of beta-catenin, which promotes the transcription of genes involved in cell proliferation and survival. In juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia, APC dysfunction can also contribute to aberrant cellular signaling, leading to myeloproliferation and leukocytosis.

partners.mechanism_chain: PTPN11 (HGNC:9520) —INCREASES→ RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (P04680); RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (P04680) —LEADS_TO→ Aberrant myeloid proliferation (HP:0001892); PIK3CA (HGNC:9535) —INCREASES→ PI3K/AKT signaling pathway (R-HSA-425542); PI3K/AKT signaling pathway (R-HSA-425542) —LEADS_TO→ Overgrowth (HP:0001510); RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (P04680) —INCREASES→ MAPK cascade (R-HSA-425543); MAPK cascade (R-HSA-425543) —LEADS_TO→ Overgrowth (HP:0001510). Gain-of-function mutations in PTPN11 (encoding SHP2) in JMML lead to constitutive activation of the RAS/MAPK signaling pathway, driving aberrant myeloid proliferation. In CLOVES syndrome, activating mutations in PIK3CA lead to overgrowth, partly through activation of the PI3K/AKT pathway, which can also influence downstream MAPK signaling. Thus, dysregulation of related signaling cascades (RAS/MAPK and PI3K/AKT) can lead to phenotypically distinct but mechanistically related outcomes.

#### 1. CBL-related disorder  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.792)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-912631, Reactome:R-HSA-1059683, Reactome:R-HSA-1236382, Reactome:R-HSA-1295596, Reactome:R-HSA-1433559)

**Proposed mechanism:** CBL (HGNC:1541) —DISRUPTS→ RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (GO:0000165); RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (GO:0000165) —INCREASES→ Leukocytosis (HP:0001894); RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (GO:0000165) —LEADS_TO→ Myeloid leukemia (HP:0005594). Gain-of-function mutations in CBL lead to dysregulation of the RAS/MAPK signaling pathway, which can manifest as myeloproliferation (myeloid leukemia) and elevated white blood cell counts (leukocytosis).

**How to falsify it:** The identification of juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia exclusively linked to loss-of-function mutations in CBL, while CBL-related disorders are solely associated with gain-of-function mutations, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs121917764)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of CBL in these conditions could lead to targeted therapies aimed at modulating RAS/MAPK signaling for both juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia and CBL-related disorders.

#### 3. gastric cancer  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.496)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-912631, Reactome:R-HSA-1236382)

**Proposed mechanism:** Activating KRAS mutation (null) —DISRUPTS→ KRAS (HGNC:6407); KRAS (HGNC:6407) —INCREASES→ MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP422); KRAS (HGNC:6407) —INCREASES→ PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP435); MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP422) —LEADS_TO→ Leukocytosis (HP:0001885); PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP435) —LEADS_TO→ Gastric Cancer (MONDO:0001056). Activating mutations in KRAS lead to its constitutive activation, which in turn promotes both the MAPK and PI3K-Akt signaling pathways. Dysregulation of the MAPK pathway contributes to the leukocytosis seen in juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia, while aberrant activation of both pathways promotes the development and progression of gastric cancer.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of activating KRAS mutations in a significant proportion of both juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia and gastric cancer cases, or the identification of distinct, non-overlapping downstream effectors for each disease, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs123456789 (hypothetical activating KRAS variant with >5% frequency in relevant populations))_

#### 7. CLOVES syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.448)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-912631, Reactome:R-HSA-1236382)

**Proposed mechanism:** PTPN11 (HGNC:9520) —INCREASES→ RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (P04680); RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (P04680) —LEADS_TO→ Aberrant myeloid proliferation (HP:0001892); PIK3CA (HGNC:9535) —INCREASES→ PI3K/AKT signaling pathway (R-HSA-425542); PI3K/AKT signaling pathway (R-HSA-425542) —LEADS_TO→ Overgrowth (HP:0001510); RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (P04680) —INCREASES→ MAPK cascade (R-HSA-425543); MAPK cascade (R-HSA-425543) —LEADS_TO→ Overgrowth (HP:0001510). Gain-of-function mutations in PTPN11 (encoding SHP2) in JMML lead to constitutive activation of the RAS/MAPK signaling pathway, driving aberrant myeloid proliferation. In CLOVES syndrome, activating mutations in PIK3CA lead to overgrowth, partly through activation of the PI3K/AKT pathway, which can also influence downstream MAPK signaling. **How to falsify it:** Demonstration that distinct signaling pathways are solely responsible for each disease, with no cross-talk or shared downstream effectors, or identification of a common pathogenic variant in PTPN11 or PIK3CA with differential penetrance or completely distinct functional consequences in the affected tissues for each disease. _(variant: A pathogenic variant in PTPN11 or PIK3CA with a significantly high allele frequency (>0.1%) in gnomAD across relevant populations, suggesting it is not a rare causal variant for either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting components of the RAS/MAPK and PI3K/AKT pathways, such as SHP2 inhibitors or PI3K inhibitors, could offer therapeutic strategies for both JMML and CLOVES syndrome, potentially requiring personalized approaches based on the specific pathway dysregulation and affected cell types.
